citation.title: New data, more corporate access? Integrity Watch EU update shows Commission leaves civil society in the dark

question: What the extended European Commission meeting-disclosure rules (December 2024) reveal about who lobbies the Commission, using the updated Integrity Watch EU platform; focus on corporate versus civil society access.
data: Integrity Watch EU data on Commission lobby meetings published by Commissioners, Cabinet Members, Directors-General and, since December 2024, all management staff (about 1100 extra officials). Meetings since the start of the new Commission mandate in December 2024; data retrieved on Monday 8 April (as stated). 5813 meetings with EU lobby organisations; 2183 published over a similar period in the previous mandate. Organisations registered in Brussels: nearly 13,000.
method: Descriptive counts of published meetings, disaggregated by individual lobbying organisation (an organisation counted for each meeting it attended). Climate-related meetings identified by subjects mentioning the EU climate agenda (at least a third of meetings); topic keywords counted (simplification, competitiveness, Green Deal, digital). Organisations are described as NGO or corporate stakeholders without a stated classification rule. No method for identifying fossil fuel lobbyists is given in this article.

definitions.term: lobbyist / lobby organisation (as counted in Integrity Watch EU)
definitions.definition: Organisations registered in the Brussels lobby register; the platform shows each organisation's lobbying footprint, with meetings disaggregated by individual organisation, so one meeting with several organisations counts once per organisation.
definitions.quote: Different organisations can attend the same meeting. As we are seeking to understand access to EU decision-makers, our platform disaggregates meeting data by individual lobbying organisation.

definitions.definition: The article treats an organisation's own label as the basis for counting it as an NGO; it notes this is not necessarily a genuine civil society representative.
definitions.quote: Only one of these three was held with an organisation that labels itself an NGO: the World Economic Forum

definitions.definition: Described as a risk arising from unbalanced stakeholder access, where only the interests of specific organisations are catered to. Not a formal definition.
definitions.quote: a lack of balanced stakeholder access could lead to policy capture, where only to the interests of specific organisations are catered to.

proxies.indicator: Number of published Commission meetings held by organisation, split between NGOs and corporate stakeholders; sectors named in the top-20 ranking.
proxies.quote: Agriculture, automobiles, chemicals, big tech and finance dominate the top ranking

proxies.indicator: Meeting subjects related to the EU climate agenda, based on the subject text because the Commission abolished its portfolio categories.
proxies.quote: In the absence of clearly defined portfolios (the Commission used to categorise meeting topics, but abolished this data point last year), the actual number could be much higher.

findings.claim: Published meetings more than doubled after the rules were extended: 5813 meetings versus 2183 in a similar period of the previous mandate.
findings.quote: EU lobby organisations held 5813 meetings since the beginning of the new Commission mandate in December 2024.

findings.claim: At least a third of published meetings concern the EU climate agenda; the true number may be higher.
findings.quote: at least a third of all published meetings have subjects related to the EU’s climate agenda.

findings.claim: Only three NGOs appear among the 20 organisations with the most Commission meetings; the top-20 is dominated by agriculture, automobiles, chemicals, big tech and finance.
findings.quote: the top 20 biggest players at the Commission only include three NGOs.

findings.claim: Corporate stakeholders dominate meetings; the new Commission held 16% of all meetings with civil society representatives.
findings.quote: this new Commission held a mere 16% of all meetings with civil society representatives.

findings.claim: The Commission President published three meetings in the new mandate, only one with a self-labelled NGO (the World Economic Forum).
findings.quote: Since the beginning of her new mandate, she’s published a mere three.

findings.claim: Authors argue (recommendation, not finding) that the Commission should ensure a balanced approach to stakeholder meetings.
findings.quote: It should do the right thing and ensure a balanced approach in meeting all stakeholders.

limitations.point: Access is not impact: meetings do not show legislative influence.
limitations.quote: access does not equal legislative impact.

limitations.point: Climate-related meeting count is a lower bound because topic categories were abolished.
limitations.quote: the actual number could be much higher.

limitations.point: Earlier analyses covered only part of meetings under the previous, narrower disclosure rules.
limitations.quote: our previous analyses could only cover the tip of the iceberg

limitations.point: Short news post: no classification rules for NGO versus corporate, no sector coding, no fossil fuel classification, no tables or figures. It does not cover COP, UNFCCC delegations, badges or conflict-of-interest rules. The fossil fuel link is only a pointer to an earlier TI EU report ('Pipelines of power').
